verdict.rationale: Hatchet is explicitly marketed as a 'durable workflow' engine with automatic retries and durability built into the queuing layer (gh-1, gh-2, gh-3), and has a dedicated Retry Policies doc (hatchet-docs-25) plus separate control-plane architecture (hatchet-docs-8/17) that decouples worker crashes from task state. However, there is no first-party or community evidence detailing exact step-level checkpointing/resume semantics after a crash, deploy, or infra failure, and no hands-on confirmation from users that a workflow actually resumes mid-execution rather than restarting. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of step-level state persistence/checkpointing, and independent/hands-on evidence confirming resume-from-last-step behavior after real crashes or deploys.
